report:
MRI of right Knee with 
-SG PD FatSat, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, CO T2W FS, AX T2W FS

> Osteoarthritis of knee joint with spur formation and subchondral bone marrow edema/cysts in tibial intercondylar eminance and lateral femorotibial joint and irregular thining of intra-articular cartilage, more severe at lateral compartment. 
> The contour of ACL in a straight line and increase signal intensity inside on F/S T2WI, in favor of degeneraiton.
> The contour of PCL appears to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> Oblitearion of lateral meniscus, reflecting tear of lateral meniscus; mild degeneration of posterior horn of medial meniscus.
> Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> A lobulated cystic lesion with internal septums in medial popliteal fossa between the tendons of the medial head of the gastrocnemius and the semimembranosus muscles, in favor of Baker's cyst, about 7 cm in length.

Impression: 
1. C/W osteoarthritis of right knee, more severe at lateral compartment.
2. Tear of lateral meniscus.
3. Muoid degeneration of ACL.
4. Mild synovitis and joint effusion in right knee; large Baker's cyst with mild perifocal edema.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

MRI LEFT KNEE

INDICATION: Assess for ligamentous injury post trauma 


Routine MRI of the left knee shows focal degenerative signal in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus with faint extension to the inferior articular surface consistent with nondisplaced tear. No lateral meniscal tear. ACL and PCL are intact. Extensor mechanism intact. Collateral ligaments are intact.

No joint effusion. No Baker's cyst. There is slight chondrosis in the medial tibial plateau with no underlying bony edema. Moderate chondrosis in the lateral tibial plateau with no underlying bony edema. No full-thickness cartilage defects. Patellofemoral joint shows focal severe chondrosis at the apex of the trochlear groove.

IMPRESSION:

Focal degenerative signal in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus with tiny inferior surfacing tear, nondisplaced. No lateral meniscal tear. No ligament tear.

Cartilage thinning in the medial lateral tibial plateaus. Tiny focus of severe chondrosis at the apex of the trochlea with 2 mm underlying subchondral edema.

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Obs. Meniscopatía lateral.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.
Meniscos de morfología y señal conservada, sin criterios de una rotura actual.
Cartílagos de los compartimentos femorotibiales y patelofemoral sin alteraciones significativas.
Tendones cuadricipital, rotuliano, tendones la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial
dentro de límites normales.
No hay alteraciones de señal de la grasa de Hoffa.
Impresión:
Examen sin hallazgos de significado patológico específico en estas secuencias.

Tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites normales.

Fibrilación marginal degenerativa del menisco medial.
Rotura compleja del cuerno anterior y parte del cuerpo del menisco lateral con leve extrusión.
Condropatía lesiones focales grado 3 del aspecto posterior de la zona de carga del cóndilo
femoral lateral. Úlceras condrales grado 1 y 2 del resto de los compartimentos femorotibiales.
Condropatía superficial de la tróclea femoral. Condropatía lesiones grado 3 de la rótula.
Leve derrame articular.
Tendinosis rotuliana proximal y cuadricipital distal.

Findings:  There is a minor knee effusion.  There is moderate thinning of the medial compartment articular cartilage with mild underlying bony change. There is mild degeneration of the distal body but no definite tears.  The lateral compartment articular cartilage is normal. Normal lateral meniscus.  There is moderate thinning of the patellar articular cartilage with focal underlying bony change in the lateral patellar facet. Normal trochlear articular cartilage.  ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  
Conclusion:: Moderate medial compartment and patellar articular cartilage degeneration. Medial meniscal degeneration but no definite evidence of tear.

Findings:  There is a moderately large knee effusion. A mild - moderate Baker's cyst is also noted. There is degenerate tearing of the posterior body and horn of the medial meniscus. Normal lateral meniscus.  Diffuse myxoid change of ACL is noted but no rupture. Normal PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  There is moderate thinning of the medial compartment articular cartilage with mild underlying bony change. The lateral compartment articular cartilage is preserved. Normal patellar articular cartilage. Moderate thinning and fraying of the trochlear articular cartilage is noted.  Conclusion: Medial compartment and trochlear articular cartilage degeneration. Degenerate tearing of the medial meniscus as described.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: 64-year-old with progressive left knee pain related to "wear and tear". Evaluate for cartilage loss. Evaluate for meniscus tear.
Comparison: No recent left lower extremity imaging available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee is acquired in 3 anatomic planes at 1.2 Tesla using a local extremity receiver coil and a noncontrast protocol.

FINDINGS:

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Osseous and articular alignment at the left knee are normal.
No fracture. No focal osseous contusion.
No evidence for a recent pivot shift mechanism.

JOINT SPACE:
There is a small left knee effusion.
There is a minimal, partially ruptured Baker's cyst.
No intra-articular bodies.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: There is a complex tear of the medial meniscus body and posterior horn with a dominant oblique undersurface component and a smaller inner margin radial component at the junction posterior horn and posterior root. There is moderate subsequent medial meniscus extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: There is diffuse partial-thickness cartilage loss all along the weightbearing region of the medial femoral condyle, with focal full-thickness cartilage loss at the medial femoral margin.
There is partial-thickness cartilage loss at the medial tibial margin.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: The lateral meniscus shows normal morphology and signal with no tear.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Articular cartilage throughout the lateral tibiofemoral compartment is normal.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
There is a small region of focal full-thickness cartilage loss at the patellar median ridge, with more diffuse partial-thickness cartilage loss extending along the medial patellar facet.
There is diffuse partial-thickness cartilage loss with deep chondral fissuring at the central femoral trochlea.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal morphology and signal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): The MCL is bowed from medial meniscus extrusion, but intact.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: The fibular-collateral ligament and anterolateral ligament are normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Intact stabilizers.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Moderate degenerative hypertrophic distal quadriceps tendinopathy, with intrasubstance degeneration at its patellar attachment and mild enthesopathy. No high-grade quadriceps tear.
Patella tendon: Normal morphology and signal with no tear or degeneration.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No significant soft tissue edema in Hoffa's fat.
A TT-TG distance is normal at 7 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
The distal iliotibial band and biceps femoris are normal.
The distal semimembranosus is normal.

SOFT TISSUES:
Neurovascular structures in the popliteal fossa are normal.
Subcutaneous soft tissues are normal. No soft tissue mass.

IMPRESSION:

1. Extensive complex medial meniscus tear with a dominant oblique undersurface component at its body and posterior horn, moderate medial meniscus extrusion, and high-grade cartilage loss on the medial femoral condyle with low-grade cartilage loss at the medial tibial margin.

2. Focal full-thickness cartilage loss at the patellar median ridge with high-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss at the central femoral trochlea.

3. Moderate degenerative hypertrophic distal quadriceps tendinopathy, with mild enthesopathy.

4. Small left knee effusion with a minimal ruptured Baker's cyst.

Diz eklemi içi sıvı miktarı hafif artmış. İç yan bağın yüzeyel bileşeni çevresindeki hafif ödem zorlanma ile ilişkili olabilir. Çapraz ve dış yan bağlar normal. Medyal menisküsün arka boynuzundaki yapı içi dejenerasyon eklem yüzeylerine yırtık biçiminde ulaşmıyor. Lateral menisküs normal. Femoral trokleanın santralin ile ve medyal femoral kondildeki kondral dejenerasyon ve kıkırdak kalınlığının %50'sini aşmayan kıkırdak kaybına femoral trokleanın santralinde subkondral medüller fibrovasküler değişiklikler eşlik ediyor. Eklem kıkırdakları ve kemikler bunun dışında normal. Ekstensör mekanizma korunmuş. Proksimal tibyofibular eklem normal. Gastrokinemyus medyal başının femoral origosu düzeyinde tendonda parsiyel yırtık ve komşuluğunda en büyüğü 1.7 cm boyutlu gangliyon kistleri. Prepatelaer cilt altı bağ dokusu ödemli. Diz ekleminin medyalinde cilt altı bağ dokusunda variköz venler izleniyor.
